summary: @servicetitan/temporal-lite preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs` in package.json. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub, unzips it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a ~727KB single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with hex-mangled identifiers and a shuffled string-array rotator (`WV8StW`). The bundle has no exported library surface and is only reachable via the preinstall dropper. The package advertises itself as a small luxon-based Temporal date wrapper, and its repository URL points to `github.com/servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib` (a UI kit) — the shipped Bun-executed payload is wholly unrelated to the advertised functionality. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: pulling in a second language runtime to execute an obfuscated payload at install time defeats Node-only scanners while running attacker-controlled code on the installer's host. The scope name and unrelated repo URL indicate scope impersonation of `@servicetitan`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
